correctness.rationale: For any fixed weight, each active (n−1)-vertex has exactly one in- and out-edge of that weight, so rotation necklaces are vertex-disjoint cycles. The complete weight-three subgraph is balanced; any balanced added weight-two multiset therefore has a common multiplicity on each weight-two necklace. If the chosen weight-two pair graph misses all three pairs of a triple, the associated weight-three necklace has no shared vertex with added cycles or other weight-three necklaces, contradicting one covering circle. Hence the complementary pair graph is triangle-free, giving at least n(n−2)/4 auxiliary edges by Mantel. Same-parity pairs give an invariant set meeting all triples. The weight-three necklace of {0,2,d} links each selected even-distance weight-two necklace d to the distance-two necklace, establishing connected balanced Eulerian existence. Mantel equality plus transitivity of cyclic shift forces the parity bipartition, and equality forces each auxiliary edge once. Explicit code verifies exact cyclic multisets and all rotation-closed optional supports for even n=6,8,10,12,14. Unbounded proof is mathematical, not by enumeration.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2012 theorem establishes Eulerian completeness of every edge of two consecutive weights; the 2013 theorem glues entire ranges and weight necklaces. Both establish existence for large specified families, not optimal selective augmentation. The separate-track exact-cover theorem minimizes number of tracks with no auxiliary restriction, which is a different cost and does not provide this single-track minimum.

originality.rationale: Comparison of actual implications places the result beyond prior theorems constructing full consecutive-weight universal cycles: covering all weight-three windows with the entire weight-two layer is not a sharp minimum among selected weight-two windows, and gives neither the Mantel bound nor the unique optimal parity support. Separate-track, weight-two-target, and necklace-transversal results do not imply the same single-circle optimum. Related primary full texts and public index records were examined. Risk remains of earlier unindexed equivalent sparse-bridge constructions.

value.rationale: The exact sparse resource needed to connect all weight-three rotation cycles into one circular universal cover is a natural one-track covering invariant. The result improves the complete two-weight construction by exactly n²/4 auxiliary windows, proves a unique optimal support instead of an arbitrary witness, and explains the sharp value by a nontrivial reduction to Mantel extremal graph rigidity. The unbounded statement and structural boundary are substantial; it does not depend on a parameter-picked small census or a renamed known table.
